Keep the bootstrap models in worker processes

Source: R/bootstrap.R
nfl4th_start_workers.Rd

add_4th_probs(bootstrap = TRUE) values every play under 100 bootstrap draws of nfl4th's models. nfl4th_start_workers() starts R processes that each load a share of the draws once and keep them in memory; while they run, each play's draws are evaluated in them in parallel, which cuts the time per play (with 11 workers, about 0.3 seconds for one play early in a game and 1 second in the last 2 minutes, against about 0.6 and 2 seconds without). nfl4th_stop_workers() stops them. They also stop when the R session ends.

The workers are separate processes (parallel::makePSOCKcluster()), so they work on every platform; starting them takes a few seconds. Without workers, everything runs in the main process.

Usage

nfl4th_start_workers(n = max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L))

nfl4th_stop_workers()

Arguments

n

Number of worker processes.

Value

The number of workers, invisibly.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
nfl4th_start_workers(4)
# ... add_4th_probs(plays, bootstrap = TRUE) ...
nfl4th_stop_workers()
} # }
